name: Supply Chain Efficiency
description: Improve logistics, fulfillment, or operational efficiency.
formula: Total logistics cost = (Units × Cost_per_unit_shipped) + Warehousing + Spoilage/waste. Saving = current - optimized.
business_contexts: e-commerce retailer optimizing last-mile delivery costs
food manufacturer reducing spoilage in cold chain
fast fashion brand renegotiating freight contracts
question_patterns: How much can annual logistics costs be reduced through optimization?
What is the total saving from reducing waste and shipping cost per unit?
Which part of the supply chain offers the highest cost reduction opportunity?
What is the annual saving from the proposed network consolidation?
solution_logic: Step 1: Calculate current shipping cost = units_shipped × current_cost_per_unit
Step 2: Calculate optimized shipping cost = units_shipped × optimized_cost_per_unit
Step 3: Calculate current waste cost = units_shipped × waste_rate_current × unit_value
Step 4: Calculate optimized waste cost = units_shipped × waste_rate_optimized × unit_value
Step 5: Calculate total annual saving = (shipping savings) + (waste savings)
key_insight: Supply chain savings compound across volume. A $2/unit improvement sounds small until you multiply it by 500,000 units.
common_mistakes: Calculating savings on a per-unit basis without scaling to total volume
Forgetting waste/spoilage as a cost category
Not separating fixed warehousing from variable shipping costs
framework_soundbite: Every cost in a supply chain is either fixed or variable. Separate them first, then find which lever moves the most at scale.
